newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Most Eurobourses climb sharply,Wall St helps.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Most Eurobourses climb sharply,Wall St helps.

text.p: Most European bourses climbed sharply on Tuesday as Wall Street opened strongly, building on the previous day's rally which wiped out "grey Friday's" losses.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened slightly but most attention was fixed on a firmer pound and a soggy Swiss franc.
Paris was the only major European bourse to lose ground. The strongest performer was Frankfurt, which soared to close floor trading 1.4 percent up, encouraged by Wall Street's rally.
"The market factors are all there," said one dealer, "I think we are back on track."
The DAX index reached 2,893.30 points at one point, again approaching the 2,914.61 record it achieved only a day before global market jitters last Friday forced it down four percent.
Many dealers are hoping for a resumption of a traditional pre-Christmas rally on the stock market and believe that if the DAX can regain the 2,900 point-level, it will trigger fresh buying interest.
"If we hit 2,900, then we will be chasing 3,000," another dealer said.

The robust performance by most European bourses was boosted by New York's recovery after turmoil sparked by comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about the "irrational exuberance" of the markets.
The Dow finished some 82 points up on Monday and made a positive start on Tuesday with technology shares making the biggest gains.

In London, the FTSE index rose 0.65 percent with investors stunned by the rapid turnaround in sentiment. At one point on Friday, slumping shares wiped 25 billion pounds ($41 billion) off the market's value.

Though investors drew comfort from Wall Street and a steady bond market, trading was thin. The market was cautious about chasing prices too high after last week's losses, which slowed bull runs on both sides of the Atlantic.
"We've tested the highs a few times over the last couple of months and each time the market has been beaten back down," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
In Paris, French stocks rose more 0.5 percent but lost the gains as investors moved in to take profits, pushing the CAC index into the minus column by mid-afternoon.
"We've had a sharp rally," said a French broker who expected the index to fall further before rebounding.
On currency markets, the dollar drifted slightly lower in quiet trading dominated by the firmer pound and the weaker Swiss franc, traders said.

Sterling grabbed traders' attention. It rose above 2.57 marks after strong demand in the Far East amid talk that Japanese banks were buying the pound as a provision for bad loans to Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel.

Analysts said it appeared that the banks had borrowed sterling in order to lend it to Eurotunnel. But as the year drew to a close, they would be left short of sterling and with positions that had to be covered.
Profit-taking took the pound back to 2.5630 marks, down from 2.5648 at the previous European close.

The Swiss franc recovered off its lows after a near brush with its 1996 low against the dollar at 1.3330 Swiss francs but traders said its weakness remained a key feature, following confirmation of a weak Swiss economy in the third quarter.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.25 yen and 1.5542 marks against 113.26 yen and 1.5556 marks in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 15.5 points higher at 4,027.1
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 6.70 at 2,249.14.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 33.76 at 2,891.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternon at $368.25 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $368.95. Silver was at $4.81, up two cents.
